clue.text: Gold fixed in trees that needed flushing out

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: the word for fixed sits inside the word for trees, so 'in' signals the insertion

parts.note: a gean is the European wild cherry tree, plural GEANS
fixed in place means steady or stable

explanation.surface: Gold has been embedded in some trees that needed washing clean.
explanation.walkthrough: The gean, a wild cherry, is a crossword favourite. 'that needed flushing out' is a fair definition because cleaning these stables was the task Hercules faced.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Hercules had to wash out King Augeas's filthy stables in one day as one of his labours.

clue.text: Direct product of Welsh factories

indicators.note: a product is something made out of raw material, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something comes straight from the factories of Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'product of' turns WELSH FACTORIES into a phrase meaning in a straight line.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes the shortest straight-line distance, so it is an adverbial synonym for directly.

clue.text: Association Football ultimately accepted by good Scots

indicators.note: the word for good in Scots takes in a letter, so being accepted by it means going inside

parts.note: GUID is the Scots form of the word good

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word football

explanation.surface: Fine Scottish people eventually took to Association Football.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Association Football' looks like one phrase; Association is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A guild is a society or union of people sharing a trade, an association.

clue.text: One in a suit seen in finest social venue

definitions.meaning: a playing card in the suit of clubs, the one ranked as one
read literally, the best of all clubs, as ace means the top one

explanation.surface: A man in a suit is spotted at the smartest club in town.
explanation.definitionFit: The card is the top club in a pack, and ace as a word for best makes it the best club too.

clue.text: Nervous about skin growth that's dark

indicators.note: the word for nervous goes round the growth, so about signals one piece enclosing the other

parts.note: shy means timid or nervous
a wart is a small growth on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about a dark growth on their skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarthy describes a dark or dusky complexion, so it is a synonym for dark.

clue.text: Old empire, so small, insubstantial to overturn

parts.note: as and so both mean in the same way, as in 'as/so good'
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: in a down clue overturning flips the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: airy means light and lacking substance

explanation.surface: An ancient empire, so slight and flimsy it was easily toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to overturn' reverses AIRY, giving YRIA.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the ancient Mesopotamian empire centred on Nineveh, a historical example of an old empire.

clue.text: One gets up early for a bit of fun

definitions.meaning: a skylark rises at dawn, and an early riser is called by this bird's name
a prank or spree done for amusement

explanation.surface: An early riser is up for some mischief.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is famous for singing at dawn, and the word also means a piece of mischief or a jape.

clue.text: So detained an ocean-going fighter briefly in place with no coast

indicators.note: detained means held inside, so the word so encloses the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter of the fighter's word is dropped

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving at sea

explanation.surface: A sailor-soldier was briefly held in a landlocked place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the last letter of the fighter's word, and 'detained' means the word So is split open around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The small republic within Italy is wholly surrounded by land, so it is a place with no coastline.

clue.text: Book course after end of year, with some earlier months abroad

indicators.note: the course comes after the year's end, so the two are placed in that order

parts.note: DEC is short for December, the final month
a line is a course or route, as in a line of action
and means with, as in 'gin and tonic'
Americans call autumn fall, the months just before December

explanation.surface: A book about a course taken late in the year, with some earlier months spent overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' tells you the American word for autumn is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of Gibbon's history of Rome and of Evelyn Waugh's first novel, so an example of a book.

clue.text: Worn out in endless attempts to save time

indicators.note: saving here means keeping safe inside, so the time letter is held within
endless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: tries are attempts

explanation.surface: Someone is exhausted by constant efforts to save time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims TRIES to TRIE, and 'to save' places T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trite means stale through overuse, hackneyed, which is a figurative sense of worn out.

clue.text: Confidence in what may follow life

definitions.meaning: insurance taken out on one's life is called life ___, the word following life

explanation.surface: A belief that something comes after life.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means certainty or self-confidence, and life assurance is a kind of insurance policy.

clue.text: No more discussion when it's time to close the book

definitions.meaning: an idiom that shuts down further argument, 'and that's that'

definitions.text: when it's time to close the book
definitions.meaning: the point at which a tale finishes, so the reader closes the book

explanation.surface: Closing the book on a matter: that is all there is to say.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said to end an argument, and literally marks the finish of a tale.

clue.text: Rule about start of lunch that may consist of many courses

definitions.text: that may consist of many courses

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for rule is reversed

parts.note: a law is a rule

indicators.note: start of points to the opening letter of lunch

explanation.surface: Someone rules on whether a lunch may have many courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' tempts you to meals; here they are layers of bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: A brick wall is built in horizontal layers of bricks called courses.

clue.text: Easy money from one stock option exercise?

parts.note: gravy is made from stock, so it is one thing a cook can do with stock
to train is to exercise

explanation.surface: Easy profit from exercising one share option, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock option' suggests finance, but the stock is a cook's.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a source of easy profit, a situation yielding money for little effort.

clue.text: Be behind counter in bank, in great style

indicators.note: the reversed piece goes inside the word for bank

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it

indicators.note: counter means running the opposite way, so the word for be behind is reversed

parts.note: to lag is to fall behind

explanation.surface: Standing behind the counter in a bank, done in fine style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter' looks like a bank counter, but it is the reversal signal; 'bank' means rely on, not a financial institution.
explanation.definitionFit: Regally means in a kingly or splendid manner, so it is a synonym for grandly.

clue.text: Roughly ignore old waterman

indicators.note: roughly suggests an approximate, rearranged version of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Treat an elderly boatman with rough disregard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' rearranges IGNORE plus OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondolier rows a Venetian boat for hire, a kind of boatman or waterman.

clue.text: Through Scottish island soldier is about to charge

indicators.note: the reversed soldier runs through the island, so it goes inside

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the soldier's letters are reversed

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier crosses a Scottish island, about to make a charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' reverses GI to IG, which goes into ARRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to bring someone before a court to answer a criminal accusation, to indict.

clue.text: Secure attention, closing British licensed premises

parts.note: to win is to secure or gain

indicators.note: the attention word closes round the British letter, holding it inside

parts.note: giving an ear means paying attention

explanation.surface: Grab attention as a British pub closes for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closing' puts B inside EAR, giving EBAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A place licensed to sell wine and other drink for consumption on site is licensed premises.

clue.text: Confirmation of purchase of extremely rare chair, say

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extreme letters, the first and last of rare
say signals that the word for chair is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a seat is a chair

explanation.surface: Proof that someone bought an extremely rare chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' means CEIPT is pronounced like SEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A receipt is the slip given to prove that goods were bought and paid for.

clue.text: Man investigating responses to a meringue

parts.note: Ivan Pavlov was the Russian scientist who studied conditioned responses in dogs

explanation.surface: A scientist tests people's reactions to a meringue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word; Pavlov is famous for dogs salivating at a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: This dessert is a meringue base topped with cream and fruit, named after a ballerina.

clue.text: Composer making arrangement for couple added note in

indicators.note: the note letter is added in among the rearranged letters
an arrangement of a piece of music, hence a reordering of these letters

explanation.surface: A composer arranges a piece for a duo, adding a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making arrangement for' rearranges COUPLE to POULEC, and N goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Poulenc was a French composer, one of the group Les Six.

clue.text: Cut round one circle and another

indicators.note: the word for cut goes round the circle shape, enclosing it

parts.note: to lop is to cut off
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: Trim around one ring and then another.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition, 'another', means another circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop is a ring or circular shape, so it is another circle beside the letter O.

clue.text: Defendant's taken in to mass, as usual

indicators.note: taken in means held inside, so the defendant's word encloses the other pieces

parts.note: the accused is the defendant in a trial; the 's is read as 'is'
taken as written
M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A defendant is led into Mass as he usually is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defendant's' reads as 'Defendant is'; 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Accustomed means customary, as in 'in his accustomed seat', so it is a synonym for usual.

clue.text: No tenderness at first in Mr Scrooge

indicators.note: no means lacking, so a letter is taken away from the title

parts.note: Mr is the short form of Mister

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of tenderness

explanation.surface: Ebenezer Scrooge shows no tenderness at the beginning of the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mr Scrooge' looks like one name, but Mr is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrooge, from Dickens, is a byword for a stingy hoarder of money, so a common noun for a skinflint.

clue.text: Sheep having nothing to eat wander off

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the sheep encloses the nothing

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Sheep with nothing to graze drift away.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to stray or ramble about, so it is a synonym for straying.

clue.text: To be a model, I pose —- time to change

indicators.note: change means altering, so the letters of the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A model strikes a pose and decides it is time for a change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges I POSE plus TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: To epitomise something is to be a perfect example of it, the embodiment.

clue.text: Confused? Worse things can happen here

definitions.meaning: bewildered or lost, an idiom for not knowing what to do
the saying 'worse things happen ___' names the ocean as the place

explanation.surface: Feeling muddled? Cheer up, it could be worse.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means bewildered, and the proverb says worse things happen on the ocean.

clue.text: Unapproachable sort of freak gadget

parts.note: remote means aloof or distant
a control freak is a kind of obsessive

explanation.surface: An aloof obsessive with a peculiar gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: The handheld device for operating a TV from a distance is a household gadget.
